Everything's in. Here's the full picture.

## Prep — done

- **mybd**: already current with origin; Dolt beads data pulled (1,462 issues, config healthy).
- **bd-main**: fast-forwarded 20 commits to `upstream/main` (now at `dbbf3a961`) and pushed to your fork. The local Entire-modified `.githooks` files were untouched (mybd-ukt3 still open but not in the way).

I reran the failed job; the babysitter patrol will resume merging once it goes green. **This red main was silently hard-blocking the entire approved merge queue** (the `PR_PREFLIGHT_BLOCK_RED_BASE` stop-the-line rule doing its job, on a false positive).

## The good

- **Enormous throughput over Jul 25–27.** ~75 coordination commits, ~38 reports, and the patrol logged **70 merges**, concentrated on the 26th. Upstream's merge log confirms it: the Harry Miller cluster (5), Vishnu J cluster (3), jjgarzella fix-merge, coffeegoddd's `bd mol` proxied capstone (#5027), your own #5013/#5046/#5082/#5094/#5098 all landed. The local sweep reports and the upstream merge log line up almost one-to-one — the sweep → patrol pipeline is genuinely working.
- **v1.1.2 hotfix shipped** and announced; the burned v1.1.1 tag was contained harmlessly.
- **The verify-before-close discipline is earning its keep**: the stub-verification sweeps found a ~30% false-positive rate on delegated "this was fixed" claims. That's a lot of wrong closes that didn't happen.
- **Patrol hardening from the retro (mybd-pqs0) works**: 15 re-arm events fired correctly, no trigger-happy blocking observed.
- **Policy landed both repos** after the #4376 post-mortem: prior-art pass is now written into upstream maintainer guidelines (#5094 merged), and the mybd overlay was refactored to import it.

## The bad

- **Two failed local verifications on claimed in-progress work**:
  - **mybd-psxg.2** (embedded↔proxied migration): one failure, `TestPersistentPreRunHonorsSkipStoreAnnotation` — looks like a real, narrow breakage worth a targeted fix.
  - **mybd-uiiu** (aux-row re-key skip-and-warn): eight failures all at ~45s — that's timeout-shaped, likely environmental (locks/parallelism) rather than the change itself, but it's gating the bead either way.
- **Broad rebase debt upstream**: roughly half of the ~105 open PRs are `CONFLICTING`. Post-#5094, rebases are explicitly maintainer work — this is now an acknowledged pile.
- **Two "no checks reported" zombies**: #4535 (Kevinwochan) and #4751 (remuscazacu), both approved, both with **zero** check runs and `UNSTABLE` merge state. The patrol has been polling them every 12 minutes for days. They likely need a trivial rebase/push to trigger CI — a human-cheap, patrol-impossible action. (The ecuthiell trio #5073/74/76, by contrast, is fully green and approved and will merge on its own once main is green again.)
- **Proxied-server mode is the active fire**: the arcaven issue/PR cluster (#5079–#5087), issue #5061 (compat-migration sweeping concurrent writes into mislabeled commits), and mybd-eolg all point at the same subsystem — which is also the psxg campaign's home turf.

## The ugly

- **#4376 is still emotionally live.** sarendipitee posted a frustrated comment on the 26th; you replied personally on the 27th. The close bead (mybd-k6zxf) says "close on/after Jul 28" — **that's tomorrow, and no agent should touch it**. The memory hold is right: a mechanical close the day after your personal apology would read terribly. Recommend you either reply/close it yourself when it feels right, or explicitly extend the grace window.
- **The all-time audit found 127 confirmed-redundant PR closes** (of 2,973), with 439 more unprobed. mybd-za009 (apologies on the 6 superseded-after-compliance PRs) is still open, and duncan4123 (mybd-q0ki6, #4561/#4736) is owed an honest disposition on work that landed then got reversed — a live supersede-risk repeat of the #4376 pattern if left to drift.

Also #5064 (your encoding-drift fix) is fully green and mergeable — it's the mainline twin of the shipped hotfix and just needs the merge call.
